verdicts.reason: Both break the original's circle-badge-with-can lockup. The cream circle is cut off at the bottom-left edge, and the can floats loose above it as a hollow outline. The headline and 'Try It' CTA are also left stranded with lots of dead orange space. A keeps the can closer to the circle, so it is a bit nearer the original grouping. B pulls them further apart and pushes the headline further right.

A has the same detached, cropped circle and hollow can as before, but it keeps the original left-to-right order: product, then headline, then the CTA on the right. B moves the 'Try It' CTA to the far left, where it sits on top of the cropped circle, so the CTA is read before the headline. B also strands the can alone at the far right, away from its badge.

A has the reversed order: the CTA is at the far left, crowding the cropped circle, and the can is isolated on the right. In B, 'Out now.' shrinks to illegible micro-text, the can shrinks and its top is clipped, and the headline drops down out of line with the CTA. B is unusable.

A's layout is broken: the circle is cropped at the edge, the can is a hollow outline separated from its badge, and the headline is pushed right. But its text is readable and the CTA stays on the right. B has illegible 'Out now.' text, a tiny clipped can at the far right, the CTA crammed against the cropped circle, and a misaligned headline.
